ce_bugs.text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Hosts have no uniqueness constraint and lookup takes an unordered first match, so duplicate rows can route imports to nondeterministic categories.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — The category lookup dereferences a missing row before its fallback, so installations without a matching embed_category override cannot run the migration.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — The backfill inserts legacy values verbatim even though the new lookup expects bare hostnames, so configured URLs with schemes or paths stop being authorized after their settings are deleted.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Host values are interpolated into SQL without quoting, so a legacy value containing an apostrophe can abort the entire upgrade instead of being backfilled.

mrv_findings.text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:4 — [P1, confidence 100] "t.string :host, null: false" — The schema has no canonical-host uniqueness invariant, so duplicate or case-variant rows can map one host to different categories while `record_for_host` resolves the winner nondeterministically with `.first`.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — [P1, confidence 100] "where(\"lower(host) = ?\", host).first" — Lookup lowercases only the stored side and discards `URI#port`, so the model accepts configurations such as `Example.COM` and `example.com:3000` that valid mixed-case or port-qualified URLs cannot reliably match.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:5 — [P1, confidence 100] "t.integer :category_id, null: false" — The host-to-category relation has neither a foreign key nor a model-level existence invariant, allowing arbitrary or deleted category IDs to persist and later be passed into topic creation as if they were valid.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:200 — [P1, confidence 100] "obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [];" — The global REST hydration path replaces every `*_ids` field with a truthy array even when none of its IDs can be resolved, deleting the original IDs and exposing `[undefined]` values to existing consumers.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — [P2, confidence 75] "where(\"lower(host) = ?\", host).first" — Every public embed authorization now incurs an uncached non-sargable database lookup with no matching functional index, creating a database bottleneck on a request path whose traffic scales with every embedded page view.

docs/tasks/task-001.md:2 — [P1, confidence 100] "Review the change." — The task supplies no acceptance criteria for category reassignment, host matching, CRUD failure behavior, or whether existing embedded topics must move, so task completion cannot be established against an explicit contract.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10 — [P2, confidence 100] "host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first" — Updating a missing or stale host ID passes nil into save_host and raises instead of returning a defined not-found response, leaving an obvious CRUD edge case unhandled.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:16 — [P2, confidence 100] "host.destroy" — Deleting a missing or concurrently removed host dereferences nil and returns a server error rather than a defined idempotent/not-found result.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6 — [P2, confidence 100] "self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')" — A create or update request with a null host crashes in the normalization callback before the format validation can produce a normal validation error.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — [P2, confidence 100] "this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => {" — The delete workflow has no rejection handler, so an API failure leaves the user without error feedback or a recoverable completion path.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — [P1, confidence 100] "WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i" — A fresh/default installation or a stale category name yields zero rows, so dereferencing row 0 aborts the migration before the intended uncategorized-category fallback can run.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — [P1, confidence 100] "execute \"INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)\"" — Direct SQL bypasses EmbeddableHost's protocol/path normalization, so legacy entries such as `https://example.com/path` migrate into rows that `record_for_host` can never match and previously allowed embeds silently stop working.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — [P1, confidence 100] "execute \"DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')\"" — The destructive settings deletion is placed in an irreversible `change` migration with no down-path reconstruction, so rollback cannot restore the legacy host/category configuration.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — [P1, confidence 100] "execute \"DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')\"" — Deleting the legacy settings in the same release that switches readers to `embeddable_hosts` violates expand-and-contract: old workers in a rolling deploy immediately see no allowed hosts, while new workers cannot start before the new table exists.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9 — [P1, confidence 100] `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` — On any installation with no persisted `embed_category` override (including the untouched default), the SELECT returns no row and `[0]['id']` raises before the migration can complete.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192 — [P2, confidence 75] "const m = /(.+)\_id(s?)$/.exec(k);" — The embedding-specific need expands the shared store's hydration contract for every REST-serialized `*_ids` field, so unrelated models can have their raw ID arrays deleted and replaced even though that behavioral change is not traceable to editing embed host/category relationships.

spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb:1 — [P3, confidence 100] "Fabricator(:embeddable_host) do" — Replacing the category fabricator file with an embedding fixture and relocating all category fixtures into an embedding-named file is unrelated test-infrastructure churn that makes non-embedding category tests depend on this feature's fixture file.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — [P1, confidence 100] "execute \"INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)\"" — A quote in the persisted embeddable_hosts setting is interpolated directly into migration SQL, enabling stored SQL injection with the database role's privileges during deployment.

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:6 — [P1, confidence 100] "expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)" — The sole test proves only inheritance, so create/update/destroy behavior, persistence, default-category handling, validation errors, and missing-record failures can all be broken while this controller spec remains green.

spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:6 — [P2, confidence 100] "expect(Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)" — The sole test never issues show/update requests or inspects serialization, so the newly introduced embedding endpoint can return the wrong host/category payload or fail authorization without this spec detecting it.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:33 — [P1, confidence 75] "let!(:embeddable_host) { Fabricate(:embeddable_host) }" — The changed integration setup creates a host with a category but every assertion checks only HTTP success, so the feature's core promise that an imported topic is assigned to that host's category is entirely unverified.

spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb:1 — [P1, confidence 75] "Fabricator(:category) do" — The embeddable-host fabricator file defines category fixtures while the embeddable host is defined in category_fabricator.rb, defeating Fabrication's name-based lazy loading and causing tests that first call Fabricate(:embeddable_host) to fail before exercising behavior.
